candidate_relations.reason: Both are benign adipocytic gastric tumors, but hibernoma (brown fat tumor) and lipoma (white fat tumor) are separate diagnostic entities with different histology and imaging characteristics; the clinical record's biopsy showing adipose tissue and the imaging features favor hibernoma as the reference diagnosis, making gastric lipoma a related but incompatible subtype
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Gastric lipoma is a benign adipocytic tumor but is a distinct entity from hibernoma; hibernoma is composed of brown fat (multivacuolated lipoblast-like cells) whereas lipoma is composed of mature white adipose tissue; the CT description of a large heterogeneous mass with fat attenuation and internal septations, combined with origin from muscularis propria, is more consistent with hibernoma than a simple lipoma

case_quality_flags: Hibernoma is an extremely rare gastric tumor; biopsy showing only 'adipose tissue' may not distinguish hibernoma from lipoma without immunohistochemistry (S100, UCP1) or detailed histology noting brown fat features
CT fat attenuation with heterogeneity and septations supports hibernoma over simple lipoma, but histologic confirmation of brown fat is required for definitive diagnosis
